caption: Sgt. Clayton Brown. The shoulder title reads 2nd Anti-Tank, RCA, above the CANADA flash and the 2nd Division patch, with a sergeant's three stripes.
Capt. Gordon Sweet, R.C.A.M.C. The cap and collar badges are the Medical Corps', and the three pips on the shoulder are a captain's.
Clayton, circled, seated in the front row of the regiment photo, September 1940. There looks to be a single stripe on his sleeve, the rank of lance-bombardier.

The whole 2nd Anti-Tank Regiment, England, September 1940. Taken by the Service Photo Co. of Pirbright, Surrey, a few miles from Farnborough. Clayton is seated in the front row, about a third of the way in from the left (close-up above). Swipe to see the whole photo. Galt Museum & Archives, P19800097000.

King George VI and Queen Elizabeth inspect Clayton's own 23rd Battery at Aldershot, March 1941. The King stands behind the 2-pounder; the Queen is beside Maj.-Gen. Victor Odlum, commander of the 2nd Canadian Division. The men in the ranks aren't named, so Clayton may be among them. Galt Museum & Archives, P19991039099.
The Jeep that took him through the war
Maj. David Currie (left of centre, holding a revolver) accepting the surrender of German troops at St. Lambert-sur-Dives, Aug. 19, 1944. Canadian Army photo, Library and Archives Canada
A 17lb gun on an English Valentine
Clayton with his self-propelled gun, Germany, 1945

The regiment's self-propelled 17-pounders on parade near Oldenburg, May 15, 1945. The "46" painted on the gun is the regiment's unit sign, the same one on the gun in Clayton's own photo. Library and Archives Canada, MIKAN 3563575

Clayton (right) on the deck of the Île de France, August 1945, with Tpr. Clifford Hooey and Sgt. Alton Morris. A Canadian Army photo, printed on the front page of the Edmonton Bulletin, Aug. 7, 1945 (Peel's Prairie Provinces, via Internet Archive). The Red Deer Advocate reran it on Aug. 15.
